I OUR FINANC PAL LETTER. ---- [FROM OUR OWN CORRESPONDENT.] 23, Old Broad-street, B.C. Dealers in stocks have had rather an anxious time during the past, but most of the anxiety was thrown away; instead ef going worse, as was generally looked for, prices recovered somewhat, and at the present time are fairly firm. Very conflicting opinions prevailed as to the probable effects of the break-up of the wheat corner at Chicago. Some dealers rook the view that it might be followed by failures, which would disturb confidence and cause a squeeze in money. In , other quarters it was considered more probable that a large amount of money which had been locked up in wheat would now be released, and find its way on the Stock Market. In the end the more hopeful view prevailed, and the latest prices from New York being good, they were quickly responded to here. Foreigners are not much affected by the American ex- citement, but they continue to drag as they have done for the past few days. Nu special development appeared in any of them, and it is evident that they are waiting for a fillip. The same may be said of the some Railways,which opened very dull, but strengthened somewhat when the American suspense began to pass away. Canadians and Americans are again a neglected market. Business in tl.ese departments has for the moment amost ceased, and at the next settlement it is likely to make a very poor show. There has been a good deal of life in miscellaneous shares; good in some cases but bad in others. At one time there was very free selling of Allsopp and Guinness, under which they weakened considerably. An impression is growing in the " House" that these shares have bad shout as much gas put into them as they can possibly hold. Cautious dealers have become very suspicious of them, and all the more so since it was discovered to what an extent the boom in them has been worked with borrowed money. Hotchkiss had a slight relapse from the high point touched a few days ago. The balance sheet of Messrs. Hutchins and Crowsley, Limited, of London, must be disappointing reading to the shareholders. Strangely enough some of the largest share- holders are in the North of England, where the knowledge of this business could only be obtained b 7 report. The dividend paid last year was 10 per cant. ; this year the business shows an actaal loss. That some drastic remedies are required goes without saying and this is admitted by the directors themselves who have called upon the manag- ing directors to make good the amount of 0,306, carried to suspense amount, but which is real ly a loss. A further item of over .£7,0n0, put down as goodwill of a business which has been carried on at a loss, and shareholders can- not eo better than appoint a committee of investigation without delay. It is necessary to point this out, as share- holders in the north of England, especially Lancashire and Yorkshire, have the largest ieterest in this business, the managing director of which has resigned, although such a step will not relieve him from liability to the share- holiers.

THE JUBILEE CELEBRATION AT RTJNCORN.

The arrangements for the celebration in Runcorn of the Queen's Jubilee are now completed, and by Monday will be issued a programme of the proceedings. In the morning, after the ringing of the church bells, a procession of friendly societies will assemble at the Market-place at ten o'clock, and will walk through the principal streets of the town. In the afternoon there will be procession of public bodies and Bundav schools, which will assemble at the Market- place at 1-30, and the members of it will, prior to walking through the town, sing the ' Old Hundreth," and the National Anthem. In the evening there will be treats at several schools, a bonfire, and a display of fireworks. A treat to the aged poor,followed by an entertainment, will be given on Wednesday. Up to the present £63 19a 5d has been obtained towards the Cottage Hospital scheme.

The Clerk read the following letter:—" House of Com- mons, June 9, 1887.—Dear Sir,—The School Fees of Non- Paupers have made inquiries about this Bill, and find that it is down for June 22 (ninth on the list), but I think there is very little chance of its coming on that day. I have not been able to find Mr. Llewellyn, who is in charge of the bill, but ether gentlemen whose names are on the 'beck of it do not seem sanguine about bringing it forward next Wednes lay week, in which ease it would prooably be Impossible to discuss it this season. I should be glad to bear of any amendment vouecommittee would like to sug- gest; it will have my very careful consideration, and I shall have much pleasure in presenting any petition to the House of Commons which you think right to frame.—l am. yours faithfully, T. C. Enwenns-Moss J. T. Allen, Esq."—The letter was referred to the General Purposes Committee.

The Clerk brought before the Board copy of a bill to amend the laws relating to machinery, and also a bill re- lating to water companies and their power to cut off the supply of water when the rates were unpaid. The first. named was referred to the General Purposes Committee and the second to the Gas and Water Committee..

div.head: GAS AND WATER CODINITTEE.
div.p: GAS AND WATER CODINITTEE.

The minutes of the Gas and Water Committee contained I the report of the engineer which stated that the machinery at Stocks Well was out of order. The rainfall for the past month had been 2015. inches. The water In stock OR the 1 25th May was 7.247,753 gallons. The illuminating power of the gas had averaged 18.68 candles. It was recommended that Mr. H. Lee's salary be advaneed from £9O to £lO5. A list of the trades:nen who refuse to pay for water for trade purposes was submitted, and instructions were given to in- sist upon payment, and if necessary, to take legal proceed-1 jogs to enforce the charges. The gas and water revenue accounts were submitted, and showed a profit of £742 7s 103 on gas and a loss of £367 19s 2d on water —Mr. Gas- kell, in moving the adoption of the minutes, explained that the loss on water account was caused by the expense of the alterations at Stocks Well. Daring the past year £l,BOO bad been paid for that purpose, so that in reality there was a profit on water of £1,500. The profit on gas making was nearly all brought about by the manufacture of sulphate of ammonia.—Mr. Taylor seconded the motion, which was carried.

THE SHIP CANAL SELECT COMMITTER.—The Committee of Selection has nominated Mr Childers, Sir John Lubbock, Mr Colman, and Mr Gillian as the Select Committee on the Ship Canal Capital Bill. Subject to the consent Mr Childers has agreed to act as chairman. The committee will meet on Thursday at noon.

Tan Cnetrzmairgns' &mtgs.—At a large representative meeting of the Chainmakers, on Friday, at Cradley Heath, it was reported that the majority of the small employers had broken faith with the operatives by reducing their wages, and it was decided to give a fortnight's notice to terminate the engagements at all the factories.

WIFE MURDER AT PENARTII.-0: boarding house keeper, named Burchall, livimg at Penarth. near Cardiff, qaatrelled with his wife on Friday afternoon. He knocked her down with a poker, and then stabbed her to the heart with a carving knife, deathbeing instantaneous. The man was afterwards arrested, and will be charged with murder to-day. Two Mate KILLED ON Tall RAILWAY,--A shocking and fatal accident occurred to Robert Nicholls, a native of Raw- tonstall, at Whitchurch station, early on Friday morning. He was shunting the Shrewsbury goods train,and standing in the six foot, when a Manchester goods train came up, and, not perceiving it, he was struck by the buffer plank, and the whole train of nearly forty carriages passed over him. When picked up be was norecognieable. He leaves a wife and two children. On Friday morning a navvy named Coulson was at work c.n the Midland Railway at Glen, near Leicester,ani, stenping oat of the way of a goods train, was knocked down by a passenger train and cut to pieces. He, too, leaves a wife and several. children.

VIENNA. FRIDAY.—Four hundred Albanians invaded the Servian village of Deb(novae, and trilled or wounded a ' number of peasants.
STEAMER BURNED AND 12 PASSENGERS DROWNED.
NEW YORK, FRIDAY—The steamer Champlain has been burned off Charlevoix, Lake Michigan. Twelve passeogers were drowned in endeavouring to escape.

The strike of the Belfast shipyard Operatives terminated on Thursday, the teastera promising to give the weekly Wages system their best consideration.
Mr. George J. Armytage, of Brighouse' was on Thursday elected Chairman of the Lancashire and Yorkshire Rail. way Company, in room of the lite Mr. JOhn Pearson.
- The seventy-third and last body has been recovered from the ticlotone Colliery, where an explos:en.recently occurred. It waa that of John NolAe, who has left a widow and five children.
At the Stockport Pole Court ,on, Wednesday, George Chapman, an ex mayor of the borough was committed for trial on the charge of having misappropriated trust Minds of considerable amount.

The exceptionally dense "aummer fog" which has been prevalent in the Irish Sea • for several, days past, led on Wednesday to another serious collision, the sinkina of the Barrow steamer Glen William and the toss of two lives.

Mr. John Bright in his reply. to Mr. Gladstone's note of the Eith instant admits that his remark about Ulster was not strictly accurate, as he wrote irons memory. He grieves that he cannot act with Mr. Gladstone as in years past, and adds that his judgment and conscience forbid it. _

MISHOCKING MURDIR.OFA Glar,--A girl named Hannah BIWA' aged nineteen, who had been working in a field art' Xismplay; near Ledbury, was found. on Wednesday evening dead in a ditch by the roadside,. stabbed in the breast. A, pensioner called Wadley, aged twenty-seven, who was seen running away from the spot, has been apprehended on sae- *ion. TEE QUEEN Ay A Barren WEEMING.—The Queen, on Tuesday attended the marriage of a daughter of one off her Helmoral tenants. Her Majesty, who was accompanied by Princess Frederica of Hanover' arrived befere the cerenaonv. which was condtreted by the Bev. James It. Middle;on, of ialennuick, and remained until its conclusion. This.is the, first wedding in ticntch form at which her Majesty has been. present. COLLAPSE OF BUILDINGS IF4 MANCHESTER : THREE PER— SONS KiLLEO —An extraordinary accident occorred on Saturday night in City-road, Manchester, whereby three lives were lost and a number of persons injured. About ten o'clock a number off people were shopping in the, establish- ment of Mr. Reavev, hoot salesman. The place is an eeeten- eive one, consisting of four shops, and nearly a dozen atten- dants were engaged in it at the time of the accident. The lower puts of the buildings were undergoing alterations, and props were fixed, here and, there to oupport the superstruc- ture. It is supposed that these wore inadevate, and that some el them were not firmly fixed, for shortly after ten o'clock the place collapsed, bringing down eleo the other three Mops, and burying those inside in a heap of ruins. Several persons were cliecoveretio alive but badly injured, and ehey were at once reepoved Cu the Infirmary. Two others were taken out of the ruins dead, and, it was feared that there were other bodies amongst the debris. The dead are Mrs. Ann .I. lif'Donough, 44, Clare-street, Hulme, who was shopping at the time, in company with her son, a lad nine years of age, who was amongst the injured, and a woman named Cheetham, 58 years of age' of Dukinfield, who was in the shop buying boots, with her daughter, a young woman, aged PA. Another' body was recevered on Monday, and identified as that of William Kirk, six years of age who was reported to the police on Saturday night as lost. It is believed that he was passim the shop when it fell.— At the police court, on Monday, several peraons were, charged with stealing boots from the ruins.. Some were fined, and some sent to prison. The coroner's inquiry was opened at Manchester, on Tuesday, before Mr. Sydney Smelton, into the death of the three victims of the disaster on Saturday night. —The coroner said that the chief point to which the jury should direct their attention was the responsibility cf the owner and necr.pier of the warehouse which fell. If the jury thought he had been criminally negligent, they would return against blm a verdict of manslaughter.—Evidence of identification rim taken, and the jury made an inspection of the building, An architect was appointed to make a special report,

The Financl Committee recommend he chArge to recommended that r the Library Committee for rent should he £57 164, bein the amount required to repay £l.OOO in 30 ye.rs at 4 per cent. Accounts, amounting to £10,795, 34d, were passed, for payment.

A STEAMER SWIM AND Two LIVES LOST.—TATI of the crew of the Barrow steamer Glen William have been landed se Liverpool by the Raccoon steamer Irrawaddy. The Irrawaidy and Glen William were in collision on Wednes- day morning off the Mull of Galloway, where the latter sank. The chief and second encineers were drowned, but all the others of the crew were saved by the Irrawaddy, The disaster happened during a dense fog. TUPORTANT Isqnx.—ln the Queen's Bench Division en Wednesday, the hearing was commenc,ad of an action by which the Lancashire and Yorkshire Railway Campany seek to recover from Andrew Knowles and Sons, Limited clams P'nsation for subsidence of the Manchester, Bolton, and Flury Canal, brv,ght about by the defendant's mining opera- tions. The facts are not disputed, but the parties are at issue on important points of law. Na less a sum than £360,000 is involved.

WIDNES PETTY BEBSIOD4S. TaituntmAT.—Before Mr. E. K. Mnspratt and Mr. EL Onkel), jun. Dirers AND DISORDERLY.—NeIIie Wright. Owen Tansey,, Cathetine Wickham, Patrick Riley, J. W. Riley, and John Mitchell were each fined for drunkenness.—Ellen Mulvey was bound over to keep the peace Tor three months for creating a disturbance in Back Major Cross-street, on the 2nd inst. WOMEN'S Qnsatitzts.—Jane Davies, a young woman who lives in Beaumont-street, summoned, Jane Thompson, a middle-aged woman, for assaulting her. A cross-summons had been issued against Davies. After bearing the evidence the Bench fined Thompson 5s and costs, and dismissed the summons against Davies.—For having. on V e 10th inst., aseaulted Elizabeth Jackson. Elizabeth Jones was fined 5s and costs.—Peter Gaffney, for using defamatory laeguage to Bridget Burke. an elderly person who lives in Marsh. street, was bound over to be of good behaviour. TALKING TO A LAMP•POST.—lienry Penketh Mather, a middle-aged man, of James-street, was charged with having been drunk and disorderly in Widnes-road, on the previous day.—P.C. Worden said the prisoner was swearing at a lamp-poet.—A fine of 5s and costs was imposed. REFITSING TO QUlT.—Thomas Tansey was summoned for having on the 10ai inst. refused to quit the Central Hotel, kept by Mr. Alfred Parkes, when requested.—He was fined 75 0.1 and costs, or ten days in default.

DEATH OF THE RUNCORN BANK MANAGER. We regret to record the death of Mr. E. A. Chorlton, manager of the Runcorn Branch of Parr's Banking Company. For a considerable time past Mr. Chorlton has been unwell, but it was not until a fortnight ago that he wss compelled to keep to his bed. Dr. McDougall was his medical attendant, and that gentleman called to his assistance first, Dr. Carruthers, of Halton. and later Dr. Glynn, of Liverpool, but their combintd skill was unavailing, and Mr. Charlton expired at half-past ten on Tuesday night. The deceased gentleman was the descendant of an old Runcorn family, his father and grandfather before him having been solicitors in the town, and by marriage he was connected with the best families in the district. He was twice married, on the first occasion to Miss Annie Cheshyre Whiteway, daughter of the late Mr. Robert Whiteway, J.P., and on the second occasion to Miss EMiIV Rigby, daughter of the late Mr. Thomas Threlfall Rigby, merchant. Although Mr. Cheri- ton had only attained %h., agent 36years, he had held the responsi` le position of manager to the Runcorn Bank for a period of eight years, having succeeded Mr, J. R. Thomp- son, who is now manager of the Cheater branch of Parr's Banking Company. Mr. Chorlton was the treasurer to the Board of Commissioners, ana to the School Board, and te nearly all public movements of a philanthropic er a social character he was always ready and willing to act in a similar capacity, and his aid was very frequently invoked. As a keen and far-seeing blsiness man, but withal courteous and obliging, Mr. Chorlton was highly respected, and in his private relations, his gentlemanly bearing, and genial char- acter, won for him the esteem and friendship of a very ex- tensive circle. A widow and three dauc.,hters are left to mourn his loss.

WARRINGTON.—These clubs played off the first of their season's engagements on Saturday, when some extraordinary batting on the part of the Liverpool team was witnessed. -After Messrs Nicholson and E H Porter had put on 38 for the first wicket, W S Patterson joined the latter, and the score was taken to 101 before Tinsley ob- tained Mr. Porter's wicket. Messrs Parr and D Q Steel made a long stand, the latter of whom played a faultless innings for 89, which included a hit out of the ground far six, one five, eight fours, six threes, and swan twos. Later on Messrs T M Patterson and Stewart-Brown put on 130 runs for the seventh wicket. The innings did not terminate until a quarter to semen, the match remaining drawn, as it was then to late for Warrington to enter upon their innings. The Liverpool innings lasted exactly four hours, and as the score was 446, it will be seen that the runs were made at the remarkable rate of over 111 per hour. The following is the score • LIVERPOOL.
